history.period: Ancient (traditional; steps to the shrine built in 1890)
history.summary: The hilltop shrine of the Mangalagiri Narasimha complex, set midway up the hill. Its signature ritual is the offering of panakam (jaggery water) poured into the deity's wide-open mouth — devotees believe the Lord drinks about half, and a gurgling sound is heard as it is offered. Legend says the Lord has been worshipped here since Satya Yuga; Rama asked Hanuman to remain as kshetrapalaka (a large Hanuman relief is carved into the rock beside the separate Lakshmi shrine above the cave temple), and a dark cave behind the shrine is believed to lead toward Undavalli. The rock steps to the shrine were built by Sri Channapragada Balaramadasu in 1890. Timings are unusual: the shrine closes by ~3 PM as it is believed gods and sages worship the Lord in the evenings. name: Sri Panakala Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
town_description: Mangalagiri ('Auspicious Hill') is a temple and handloom town in Guntur district on the Guntur-Vijayawada highway, closer to Vijayawada. It is famous for the twin Narasimha temples — the hilltop Panakala shrine and the downhill Lakshmi Narasimha temple with its 153-ft gopuram — and for Mangalagiri cotton saris and dress material woven on its handlooms.

travel.railway: Mangalagiri railway station; Vijayawada Junction (~12 km)
travel.road: On the Guntur-Vijayawada highway; steep rock steps and a ghat road lead up to the hilltop shrine

visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM - 3:00 PM; no evening darshan (some sources say till 4:30 PM — verify)
